feature_under_test: bounded MySQL connection stall and resumption while a real-Chrome request is in flight

environment.mysql: ephemeral MySQL 8.4 with separate non-root migration and runtime accounts
processes: one Atoll Server process kept alive throughout the injected database stall
one execution daemon kept alive throughout the injected database stall after its real Chrome request reached the origin

fault_cut.browser_state_before_cut: Attempt running, no Artifact persisted, and controlled origin accepted exactly one document request
fault_cut.cut: docker pause the ephemeral MySQL container for seven seconds while Server and the execution daemon remain alive, then docker unpause it

invariants: the database is paused only after the Attempt is running, the real request has reached the origin, and no Artifact exists
Server and the execution daemon survive the full database stall after a real Chrome request has reached the origin
the original Attempt resumes and succeeds after MySQL returns; no replacement Attempt or attempt_recovered dispatch is created
the controlled website receives exactly one document request, so database recovery does not become a refetch
the original Attempt persists exactly one DOM response, one effect trace and one BackfillOutput
all Permits and execution dispatches settle without manual database mutation
a final normal Server restart preserves both Resource reads and the completed state
non_claims: MySQL failover, primary/replica promotion, or a dropped and re-established TCP connection
a remote database or long database outage
simultaneous Atoll Server and MySQL failure
remote cloud or object-storage provider behavior
third-party JavaScript, authentication, anti-bot or availability behavior

acceptance.gate: P9 MySQL unavailable during an in-flight real-Chrome request
